_readme: M1 (not the spike) — SQLite promoted to the default (only) chunk store; MAST_CHUNK_STORE
env gate and Lance chunk-table usage retired from every production write/read path. Compares
against eval/store-spike.json's numbers (same corpora, same methodology where possible) and
re-runs the read-set correctness diff now that the chunk_id collision fix (store-spike.json's
defects.chunk_id_collision) has landed.
Design decision (see packages/mast/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md Stage 2 'M1 result' for full
rationale): chunks live IN graph.db's `chunks` table, NOT a separate chunks.db as the spike
used. graph/populate.ts's populateFile writes chunks in the SAME per-file db.transaction() as
symbols/edges/imports/chunk_fts — proven by graph/__tests__/storage.test.ts's atomicity test
(a failing chunk writer rolls back the whole transaction, zero orphaned rows anywhere).
Part A (write path) regenerated on FRESH state dirs (mast-bench/m1-{common,nest,directus}-
sqlite) — mast-state/, baseline-state/, f1-state/, audit2/ were NOT touched, per instructions.
Part B (read-set diff) could NOT reuse the 2-day-old mast-state Lance reference as originally
planned: `nest`'s live git checkout had uncommitted edits to 14 files (packages/core/injector/
*, etc.) from earlier E7 concurrency-test sessions, which shifts chunk_fts's corpus-wide BM25
statistics independent of the store migration (store-spike.json's own
part_b_read_path.score_drift_explanation documented this exact mechanism) — comparing against
a stale reference would have produced non-attributable diffs. Re-ran instead as a single-parse-
pass, dual-write comparison: one walkProject+extractFile pass over the CURRENT nest snapshot
feeds a Lance chunk table AND the SQLite chunks table from byte-identical Chunk[] input, then
hybridSearch/getChunksByFilePath/collectPotentialMatchCandidates are diffed with ONLY the
chunk-store backend swapped (same db, same FTS, same symbols/edges — see
/private/tmp/.../m1-same-build-diff.mjs, not checked in; script content summarized in the
'read_set_diff' section below). This isolates the comparison to the store's own read/write
behaviour and is immune to corpus drift.
To regenerate part A: pnpm -F mast build; mast index <corpus> --phase1-only --state-dir
<fresh-dir> (no env var — SQLite is unconditional now).

part_a_write_path._note: duration_ms is runIndex's own Date.now()-startMs (whole --phase1-only pipeline), matching store-spike.json's methodology. wall_s is process-external.

corpora.label: nest (full)
corpora.note: chunk_count 5030 == the PRE-migration Lance build's count exactly (mast-state/index.json), and 0 parse_errors/write_errors — confirms the chunk_id-collision defect (store-spike.json defects.chunk_id_collision, real case: probe-lab/lab3.ts) is fixed; the spike's sqlite arm had chunk_count 5022 + 1 parse_error from that same defect, pre-fix.

corpora.label: directus (copy at mast-bench/directus, not indexed in place)
corpora.note: chunk_count 7198 vs spike's lance-arm 7214 / sqlite-arm 7174 — plausible minor corpus drift in the directus copy between spike capture and this run (0 parse_errors here rules out a chunk_id-collision recurrence); not investigated further, out of scope for M1.

verdict.wall_ceiling_82s: NOT FIRED on all three corpora (max 11s, well under)
verdict.duration_vs_spike_sqlite_arm: within +8%..+22% of the spike's own sqlite-arm numbers on all three corpora — consistent with system load noise, not a regression. All three remain 60-70x faster than the pre-migration Lance arm.
verdict.state_bytes_vs_lance_baseline: nest: 194-233MB (Lance, per IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md Stage 2 / mast-state) -> 17MB (13x-14x smaller); directus: 409MB -> 33MB (12x smaller) — matches store-spike.json's ~17MB nest prediction almost exactly.

part_b_read_set_diff._note: Single-parse-pass dual-write comparison (see _readme) over the CURRENT nest snapshot (1,338 files, 0 parse errors) — corpus-drift-free by construction. mast_exports/mast_callers compared via their actual chunk-store-dependent primitives (getChunksByFilePath / collectPotentialMatchCandidates); their store-INDEPENDENT fields (extractFileSignatures output, FTS ranking) are already identical by construction since both arms share one graph.db.
part_b_read_set_diff.verdict: 0 content differences across all 4 comparison groups (5,030 + 20 + 5 + 5 = 5,060 individual comparisons). Per the task brief: the chunk_id collision fix removed the known cause of divergence, so any content diff now would be a NEW defect — none found.

corpus_drift_note.observed: The live nest/ checkout at mast-bench/nest had uncommitted edits to 14 files (packages/core/injector/{compiler,container,injector,instance-links-host,instance-loader,instance-wrapper,internal-providers-storage,module,module-ref,modules-container,settlement-signal}.ts, packages/core/adapters/http-adapter.ts, packages/core/router/router-proxy.ts, packages/microservices/nest-microservice.ts, packages/websockets/web-sockets-controller.ts), most plausibly artifacts of an earlier E7 concurrency-test session (IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md Stage 4/F11: 'N separate mast serve processes... each editing its own file and re-querying it').
corpus_drift_note.impact: Caused the originally-planned mast-state (Lance, captured 2026-07-26) vs freshly-built SQLite arm comparison to show 27/30 non-identical results — traced to BM25 score/tie-order drift from the corpus-size delta (1337 vs 1338 files), the exact mechanism store-spike.json's part_b_read_path.score_drift_explanation already documented as benign. NOT a migration defect — reported per instructions ('do not mistake it for a migration defect, and say so if you see it') and NOT papered over: the single-parse-pass dual-write methodology above sidesteps the confound entirely and is the authoritative read-set result.
corpus_drift_note.walkProject_nondeterminism: Separately, IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md Stage 4/D1 documents ~+-4/3,940 edge nondeterminism from walkProject's unsorted output (fast-glob readdir order) — out of scope for M1 (D1 explicitly not done here), not observed to materially affect this diff since the dual-write script uses one walk for both arms.
